alerts.title: AKI likely pre-renal, not TDF toxicity
alerts.message: Guidelines list acute kidney injury as a TDF toxicity and recommend LFTs and RFTs when deranged. Patient has creatinine 2.4 (from 0.9) on TDF. However, strong evidence favours non-drug attribution: 5 days of severe vomiting and diarrhoea with dehydration, household contacts with same illness, urea:creatinine ratio 24:1 suggesting pre-renal AKI, and urinalysis showing no protein or glucose (TDF nephrotoxicity typically causes proximal tubular dysfunction with proteinuria/glycosuria). Permanent TDF discontinuation may be unnecessary if renal function recovers with fluid resuscitation.

evidence.recommended_action: Resuscitate with IV fluids and reassess renal function before deciding on permanent TDF discontinuation. If creatinine normalises, TDF may be continued with monitoring.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring gap during AKI
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring every 12 months for patients on TDF. Patient's last documented creatinine was 375 days ago. Current AKI with creatinine 2.4 necessitates repeat renal function tests after resuscitation to track recovery. No eGFR has been documented. Ongoing renal monitoring is essential given TDF nephrotoxicity risk and current acute injury.

evidence.recommended_action: Check serum creatinine and eGFR after IV fluid resuscitation, then serially until normalised. Resume annual TDF renal monitoring once stable.

alerts.title: Hypokalamia and hyponatraemia need correction
alerts.message: Patient has potassium 3.1 mmol/L and sodium 132 mmol/L alongside severe dehydration and AKI. These electrolyte abnormalities are consistent with gastrointestinal losses from gastroenteritis. TDF can cause renal tubular dysfunction leading to electrolyte wasting, but the absence of proteinuria and glycosuria on urinalysis makes TDF-related Fanconi syndrome unlikely. Hypokalamia with AKI increases risk of cardiac arrhythmia and requires prompt correction alongside fluid resuscitation.

evidence.recommended_action: Replace potassium urgently and correct sodium gradually. Monitor electrolytes every 6–12 hours until stable. Reassess after fluid resuscitation.
